title: Largest Land Animals in the World
metric_label: Typical adult male weight · wild species only
source_line: Sources: IUCN Red List, peer-reviewed studies, zoo & reference works

layout.image_prefer: the whole animal clearly visible (adult, ideally a male), in its natural wild habitat, sharp, eye-level, strong natural light (golden hour or clear day); a wild animal rather than a zoo enclosure; the CORRECT species, not a domestic form or a look-alike relative; landscape or portrait both fine

music_credit: Music: original instrumental generated for this channel with Suno (job 101bce70, clips 11cce2f0 + b2fcbabf).
scope_note: Ranked by typical adult male weight of living wild species (IUCN taxonomy); where sources give a range, we use its midpoint. Excluded: domestic animals, marine mammals, crocodilians, and wild Bactrian camels (no published weights separate wild males from domestic ones). Hippos and polar bears are included. Flags mark the country with the largest wild population; continents follow UN M49. Ranks within ~5% are effectively ties. Forest elephant (2–4.5 t) and gaur (0.65–1.5 t) weights are estimates. Low-confidence flags: giraffe, giant eland, bongo, common eland, European bison.

items.name: African Bush Elephant
items.subtitle: Sub-Saharan Africa

source.name: Larramendi 2016, Acta Palaeontologica Polonica 61(3):537-574 (peer-reviewed)
source.text: Average fully-grown male in good condition (3.20 m at shoulder) ~6,000 kg; ~90% of bulls 5.2-6.9 t (Table 8)

cross_check.source_name: Owen-Smith 2024, 'Megaherbivores', Encyclopedia of Biodiversity 3rd ed., Table 3 (male 5000-8000 kg, midpoint)

stronghold.evidence: 2022 KAZA aerial survey: Botswana 131,909 (largest), Zimbabwe 65,028 second; consistent with 2015 GEC 130,451

wild_population.source_name: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance Library fact sheet citing Chase et al. 2016 (Great Elephant Census, 18 of 30+ range states)

max_mass.text: Bull shot in Angola 1974, 3.96 m at shoulder (forefoot circumference 180 cm); 10.4 t is an allometric estimate, not a weighing; older Wood 1982 estimate ~12.3 t

items.image_hint: adult bull African bush (savanna) elephant in the wild, big fan-shaped ears, long tusks, full body on open savanna; NOT an Asian elephant, NOT a forest elephant
items.notes: No official species-level population estimate yet: AfESG 2016 Status Report gave ~415,428 for BOTH African species combined (Wikipedia attributes it to bush elephant alone); AfESG savanna report announced for 2026 but not found published. 350,000+ is a partial-coverage floor (GEC 2016). IUCN assessment published 2021 (assessed 2020), amended 2022. Mass cross-check 6,500 vs 6,000 = 8% (ok).

items.name: Asian Elephant
items.subtitle: South & Southeast Asia

source.name: Larramendi 2016, Acta Palaeontologica Polonica 61(3):537-574 (peer-reviewed)
source.text: Average-sized male (275 cm) in optimal conditions ~4,000 kg; ~90% of bulls 3.5-4.6 t

cross_check.source_name: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance Library fact sheet (avg male ~3,600 kg)

stronghold.evidence: IUCN 2020: India 29,964 of ~50,000; India's first DNA-based count (WII, Oct 2025): 22,446 (18,225-26,645) - still by far the largest

wild_population.source_name: IUCN Red List assessment (Williams et al. 2020), citing Menon & Tiwari 2019: 48,323-51,680 wild

max_mass.text: Tallest on record: bull shot in Assam, India, 1924, est. 3.43 m at shoulder; ~7 t is an allometric estimate, not a weighing

items.image_hint: adult male Asian elephant (tusker) in the wild, small rounded ears, twin-domed head, full body; NOT an African elephant; no riders, no chains, no temple decorations
items.notes: Global figure likely overstated now: it uses India 29,964 (2017), but India's 2025 DNA census (https://www.civilsdaily.com/news/status-of-elephants-in-india-report-2025/) gives 22,446 (new method, not directly comparable) -> global total may now be ~40,000-45,000 (inference). Mass cross-check SDZG 3,600 vs 4,000 = 10% (borderline); Owen-Smith 2024 gives 4,000-5,400. Larramendi notes many published Asian elephant weights come from obese captive animals. IUCN assessed 18 Sep 2019, published 2020. Captive 'up to 6,000 kg' (SDZG) not used.

items.name: White Rhinoceros
items.subtitle: Southern & East Africa

source.name: Owen-Smith 2024, 'Megaherbivores', Encyclopedia of Biodiversity 3rd ed., Table 3
source.text: Adult male body mass 2200-2400 kg (female 1600-1800)

cross_check.source_name: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance Library fact sheet (males c. 2,300 kg)

stronghold.evidence: End-2024: South Africa 12,082 of 15,752 (76.7%); Namibia 1,500, Kenya 1,043

wild_population.source_name: CITES CoP20 Doc.84 Annex 3 (IUCN SSC AfRSG/AsRSG & TRAFFIC 2025), Tables 3 & 5 (end-2024; -11.2% vs 2023)

items.image_hint: adult white (square-lipped) rhinoceros in the wild, wide square mouth, large shoulder hump, two horns, full body on grassland; NOT a black rhino
items.notes: Northern white rhino (C. s. cottoni): only 2 left (Kenya). IUCN 2020: 10,080 mature individuals; assessed 6 Jan 2020. No reliable individual max weight found (ADW range up to 3,600 kg; Wikipedia's 4,500 kg unsourced). ~1,299 more in zoos outside Africa. Shoulder height 1.70-1.85 m (SDZG, both sexes). Daily Maverick: SA white rhinos -15% in 2024 (14,074 incl. other counts).

items.name: Indian Rhinoceros
items.subtitle: India & Nepal

source.name: Owen-Smith 2024, 'Megaherbivores', Encyclopedia of Biodiversity 3rd ed., Table 3
source.text: Adult male body mass 2100 kg (female 1600 kg)

cross_check.source_name: Animal Diversity Web (adult males 2,200 kg on average; females 1,600)

stronghold.evidence: India 3,323 vs Nepal 752 (early 2025); Kaziranga NP alone 2,613

wild_population.source_name: CITES CoP20 Doc.84 Annex 3 (IUCN SSC AfRSG/AsRSG & TRAFFIC 2025), Tables 3 & 5 (early 2025: India 3,323, Nepal 752)

items.image_hint: greater one-horned (Indian) rhinoceros in the wild, armour-plated skin folds, single horn, full body in tall grass or wetland (e.g. Kaziranga, Chitwan)
items.notes: IUCN assessed 6 Dec 2018 (published 2019): 2,100-2,200 mature individuals. Nepal figure 752 is from the 2021 count; 2025 count postponed, 2026 DNA-based count planned (no result found). ADW shoulder height males 1.70-1.86 m (midpoint used). No reliable individual max weight found.

items.name: African Forest Elephant
items.subtitle: Central & West Africa

source.name: Larramendi 2016, Acta Palaeontologica Polonica 61(3):537-574 (peer-reviewed)
source.text: No study has weighed forest elephants; average male of 220 cm at shoulder 'should be around 2000 kg' (~90% 1.7-2.3 t)

cross_check.source_name: Owen-Smith 2024, 'Megaherbivores', Encyclopedia of Biodiversity 3rd ed., Table 3 (male 4500 kg, female 2500 kg)

stronghold.evidence: Gabon holds 66% of the global forest elephant population, Rep. of Congo 19% (AFESR 2024); WCS 2021 DNA survey: ~95,000 in Gabon

wild_population.source_name: IUCN press release 27 Nov 2025 on African Forest Elephant Status Report 2024 (surveys 2016-2022; 95% CI 99,343-172,297)

items.image_hint: African forest elephant in the wild, rounder oval ears, straight downward-pointing tusks, in a rainforest clearing (bai) e.g. Dzanga Bai; NOT a savanna elephant
items.notes: MASS CONFLICT >10%: Larramendi 2016 ~2.0 t vs Owen-Smith 2024 table 4.5 t vs Grubb et al. 2000 (via Wikipedia) 4-7 t for bulls. No direct weighings exist; highly uncertain. Female mass not reliably sourced (Owen-Smith 2,500 kg) -> null. Population rise vs 2016 reflects better survey coverage, not growth (IUCN). IUCN assessed 13 Nov 2020, published 2021.

items.name: Hippopotamus
items.subtitle: Sub-Saharan Africa

source.name: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance Library hippo fact sheet
source.text: Males average 1,546 kg, females 1,385 kg (Klingel 2013, Mammals of Africa)

cross_check.source_name: Wikipedia 'Hippopotamus' (mean bull 1.48 t, citing Owen-Smith); Owen-Smith 2024 Table 3 gives male 1500-2600 kg

stronghold.evidence: 2005-2008 surveys estimated 40,060 hippos in Zambia (62% in Luangwa system); Tanzania ~20,000 (2001-based estimate). Candidates: Zambia, Tanzania

wild_population.source_name: IUCN Red List (Lewison & Pluhacek 2017), as summarised by Wikipedia

max_mass.text: Maximum male weight 3,200 kg given by Kingdon 1979 (p.256); claims of 4,500 kg (captive Munich male, traced to Bere 1959) flagged as possibly inaccurate
max_mass.source_name: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance Library hippo fact sheet

items.image_hint: adult common hippopotamus in the wild, whole body visible (on land or riverbank), ideally mouth open showing tusks; NOT a pygmy hippo
items.notes: Mass: Owen-Smith 2024 range 1,500-2,600 looks like mean-to-max, so its midpoint (2,050) would overstate (>10% from 1,546). Max conflict: Kingdon 3,200 kg vs Klingel ~2,065 kg vs Wikipedia 2,660 kg. Zambia/Tanzania counts dated; range states argued at CITES CoP19 that IUCN 2017 underestimated several countries. Trend 'stable' per Wikipedia summary of IUCN 2017, not verified on IUCN page. Height 1.50-1.65 m (SDZG, Kingdon 1979; labelled height, not explicitly shoulder). Value 122,500 = midpoint.

items.name: Javan Rhinoceros
items.subtitle: Ujung Kulon, Indonesia

source.name: Owen-Smith 2024, 'Megaherbivores', Encyclopedia of Biodiversity 3rd ed., Table 3
source.text: Adult body mass 1300 kg for both sexes

cross_check.source_name: Animal Diversity Web (both sexes 1,500-2,000 kg, midpoint)

stronghold.evidence: Only surviving population: Ujung Kulon National Park, Java

wild_population.source_name: CITES CoP20 Doc.84 Annex 3 (IUCN SSC AfRSG/AsRSG & TRAFFIC 2025), Tables 3 & 5 (early 2025; 26 lost to poaching 2019-2023 per IUCN)

items.image_hint: Javan rhinoceros (Rhinoceros sondaicus) — extremely rare, photos come from Ujung Kulon National Park (camera traps or wallow photos); NOT an Indian rhino; accept the best real photo available
items.notes: MASS CONFLICT >10%: Owen-Smith 1,300 kg vs ADW 1,500-2,000 kg vs Handbook of Mammals of the World 1,200-1,500 kg (search snippet only); few wild weighings, ADW notes females may be larger. IUCN: CR, Ellis & Talukdar 2020 (seen on Rhino Resource Center author list); exact Red List URL/assessment ID and trend not verified (iucnredlist.org returned 403). Population conflict: IRF 2022 high estimate 76; an Indonesian 2026 news snippet (rri.co.id) mentions 80-100 - unverified; CITES/IUCN 2025 figure ~50 used. Taxonomy: Nardelli & Heissig (ZooKeys 2025) proposed genus Eurhinoceros (E. sondaicus) - a proposal, not adopted by IUCN.

items.name: Giraffe
items.subtitle: Sub-Saharan Africa

source.name: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance Library giraffe fact sheet
source.text: Male mean 1,191.8 kg (+/-1 SD 973-1,395); female 828.4 kg (Ciofolo & Le Pendu 2013, n=15-18)

cross_check.source_name: Owen-Smith 2024, 'Megaherbivores', Encyclopedia of Biodiversity 3rd ed., Table 3 (male 1200-1400 kg, midpoint)

stronghold.evidence: Kenya 34,240 (2021 national census); South Africa ~30,000 (2025 report); Tanzania ~28,850 (TAWIRI aerial data, year unclear). Candidates: Kenya, South Africa, Tanzania

wild_population.source_name: GCF State of Giraffe 2025 as reported in CMS COP15 Doc.31.2.5 (species: Masai 43,926; Northern 7,037; Reticulated 20,901; Southern 68,837 per search snippets)

items.image_hint: adult bull giraffe in the wild, the whole animal from hooves to ossicones visible, on savanna
items.notes: TAXONOMY: IUCN SSC Giraffe & Okapi SG (Aug 2025) recognised 4 species (Northern G. camelopardalis, Reticulated G. reticulata, Masai G. tippelskirchi, Southern G. giraffa) and 7 subspecies; Red List still lists one species (VU, 2016 assessment amended 2018, ~97,500 animals then); per-species Red List assessments planned for 2026 (CMS doc). If the split is used, the ranking entry may need to be one species (e.g. Southern giraffe, most numerous). Trend 'decreasing' per 2016 listing rationale (~36-40% decline 1985-2015, media), not read on IUCN page; GCF 2025 says 3 of 4 species now stable/increasing. Max mass: Larramendi 2016 says largest bulls ~1.2-1.5 t (no individual record) -> null; 1,511.6 kg (Mitchell et al.) and 1,900 kg claims not verified. Stronghold uncertain: figures from different years/methods.

items.name: Black Rhinoceros
items.subtitle: Southern & East Africa

source.name: Owen-Smith 2024, 'Megaherbivores', Encyclopedia of Biodiversity 3rd ed., Table 3
source.text: Adult body mass 1000-1300 kg for both males and females

cross_check.source_name: Animal Diversity Web (800-1,400 kg; males a little larger)

stronghold.evidence: End-2024: South Africa 2,307, Namibia 2,098, Kenya 1,059, Zimbabwe 784

wild_population.source_name: CITES CoP20 Doc.84 Annex 3 (IUCN SSC AfRSG/AsRSG & TRAFFIC 2025), Tables 3 & 5 (end-2024; +5.2% vs 2023)

items.image_hint: black (hook-lipped) rhinoceros in the wild, pointed prehensile upper lip, two horns, full body; NOT a white rhino
items.notes: Stronghold close call: SA 2,307 vs Namibia 2,098 (Namibia uses sample counts with CIs; older reports called Namibia the largest). IUCN assessed 14 Jan 2020: 3,142 mature individuals; subspecies D. b. bicornis downlisted to NT. Sexes similar in size. SDZG gives 1,000-1,800 kg. No reliable max record.

items.name: Gaur
items.subtitle: South & Southeast Asia

source.name: Nowak 1999, Walker's Mammals of the World (male range, via Wikipedia)
source.text: Walker's Mammals of the World: adult males 588-1,500 kg, females 440-1,000 kg (male-specific; read via Wikipedia 'Gaur')

cross_check.source_name: Handbook of the Mammals of the World vol. 2 (650-1000 kg, sexes not separated; midpoint)

stronghold.evidence: IUCN 评估文本：Ranjitsinh (1997) 估计印度 12,000–22,000 头，而全球 13,000–30,000 头；西高止山为最大据点；Wikipedia（引 IUCN 2016）称多数在印度

wild_population.source_name: IUCN Red List 2016 (Duckworth et al.), via Wikipedia; IUCN 2008 text (ESABII) gives 13,000–30,000 total / 5,200–18,000 mature

max_mass.text: 未找到具体称重记录；常见说法“公牛可达 1,500 kg”（中国种群，Smith & Xie 2008 经 Wikipedia 转引）只是范围上限，不作为可靠个体记录

items.image_hint: adult bull gaur (Indian bison) in the wild, massive muscular dorsal ridge, white 'stockings' on the legs, full body in Indian forest; NOT domestic cattle, NOT gayal/mithun
items.notes: 雄性体重口径冲突 >10%：AWCSG 给 440–1,000 kg（雌雄合并），Wikipedia/Nowak 给雄性 588–1,500 kg（中点 1,044）；旧版 Wikipedia 另有“平均 650–1,000 kg、偶见 1,500 kg”。未能打开 Walker's 原书核对，雄性典型值建议按 ~1,000 kg 量级谨慎使用。马来亚野牛（seladang）与印度野牛均归本种。家养型大额牛（gayal/mithun, Bos frontalis）不收。IUCN 物种页（iucnredlist.org）在本次调研中返回 403/Cloudflare，无法直接打开；类别/年份依据 IUCN 评估 DOI 引用（Wikipedia 引文）、IUCN SSC 专家组页面、ESABII（日本环境省生物多样性中心转载的 IUCN 评估文本）与 Mammal Diversity Database 交叉核对。 ｜主会话改动：复审 N2：HMW 650–1000 不分性别（中点 825 低估雄性）；改回唯一能找到的雄性专属范围（Walker's 588–1500，经维基读取，tier=secondary），HMW 作交叉核对（-21%）。差异 > 10% 已记 ｜第 3 轮审片 R3-M1：未找到雄性体重的一手出处（Ahrestani 2018 原文取不到），保留中点 1,044 并在卡上首位标「Estimates: 650–1,500 kg」，描述框口径说明写明是估计值

items.name: Wild Yak
items.subtitle: Tibetan Plateau

source.name: Leslie & Schaller 2009, Mammalian Species 836 (Bos grunniens and Bos mutus)
source.text: Body mass of adult male wild yaks estimated at >800 kg (Engelmann 1938), as high as 1,000 kg (Schäfer 1937; Wiener et al. 2003) and 1,200 kg (Lu 2000); females about 350 kg (Schaller 1998)

cross_check.source_name: IUCN SSC Asian Wild Cattle Specialist Group – Wild yak（500–1,200 kg，雌雄合并，中点）

stronghold.evidence: 分布于中国（藏北、青海西部、新疆南缘）、印度拉达克（小种群）及尼泊尔（2014 重新发现）；羌塘保护区约 7,000–7,500 头

wild_population.source_name: Nepal Shey Phoksundo NP / WWF wild yak survey report 2024（引 Buzzard & Berger 2016 IUCN：全球 <10,000 成熟个体）；AWCSG 与 Leslie & Schaller 2009：野外 <15,000 头

max_mass.text: 1,200 kg 为中国文献估计上限（Lu 2000; Lu & Li 1994），非称重记录

items.image_hint: WILD yak (Bos mutus) on the Tibetan plateau / Chang Tang, uniformly blackish-brown, long skirt of hair, wild herd — NOT a domestic yak (no white patches, no saddles, no ropes, no herders)
items.notes: 雄性体重均为早期估计而非系统称重；雌性约为大雄性的三分之一。家养牦牛（Bos grunniens）不收。IUCN 2016 人口趋势未能直接核实，填 unknown。尼泊尔调查报告 URL 来自搜索结果，未逐页打开。IUCN 物种页（iucnredlist.org）在本次调研中返回 403/Cloudflare，无法直接打开；类别/年份依据 IUCN 评估 DOI 引用（Wikipedia 引文）、IUCN SSC 专家组页面、ESABII（日本环境省生物多样性中心转载的 IUCN 评估文本）与 Mammal Diversity Database 交叉核对。

items.name: Wild Water Buffalo
items.subtitle: India, Nepal & Thailand

source.name: IUCN SSC Asian Wild Cattle Specialist Group – Wild water buffalo
source.text: Body mass 700–1,200 kg; males typically around 20% larger than females

cross_check.source_name: Wikipedia: Wild water buffalo（600–1,200 kg，引 Aryal et al. 2011；3 头圈养个体平均 900 kg）

items.name: American Bison

insights.text: Each flag marks the country where most of that species lives in the wild.
Just missed the cut at #31: the Galápagos giant tortoise, at about 295 kg.
Saltwater crocodiles (males ~460 kg) would rank here, but we count crocodiles as aquatic.
The kouprey (~750 kg) would rank near here, but none has been confirmed alive in decades.
From here on, every typical adult male weighs a tonne or more.
Giraffe experts now recognise 4 species; the IUCN Red List still lists just one.
